text:
sana_kobayashi: FYI I'm onboarding aorta-v1 (q5) to staging. Quick smoke showed unexpected token boundary changes for mixed katakana+kanji when there's an invisible joiner (ZWJ U+200D) or ZWSP U+200B between clusters. Embedding similarity to fp16 baseline drops on short retrieval queries. Anyone seen this pattern after quant exports?

mike_han: Can you paste a tiny repro and which tokenizer/version?

sana_kobayashi: Using rn-tokenizer v2.5.0 vendored. Minimal repro below. Note I replaced literal chars with escapes for readability.

```
# fp16
rn_tokenizer inspect --model aorta-v1 --mode fp16 --text "\u30ab\u30ca\u200d\u6f22"
# q5
rn_tokenizer inspect --model aorta-v1 --mode q5 --text "\u30ab\u30ca\u200d\u6f22"
```

fp16 -> tokens ["\u30ab\u30ca", "\u6f22"] ids [4012, 9872]
q5   -> tokens ["\u30ab\u30ca\u200d", "\u6f22"] ids [4012, 49801]

olga_petrov: That looks like normalization/fast-tokenize divergence. Did the q5 runtime build use TOK_NORMALIZE=fast or a different grapheme segmentation lib? Also 49801 being > vocab size suggests extension-slot remap in the packer.

sana_kobayashi: Confirmed: q5 image built with TOKENIZE_FAST=1 (to hit lower p95). fp16 uses TOKENIZE_FAST=0. Vocab file identical across artifacts.

mike_han: How large is the impact? Affected sample count and downstream metric?

sana_kobayashi: Short JP retrieval set (n=300, lots of katakana+kanji): ~20% show boundary attach for ZWJ/ZWSP. For those, embedding cosine median goes 0.94 -> 0.76 and retrieval recall@10 drops ~5.5 points. Translation BLEU barely moves (~0.2) because detok normalizes in pipeline.

deploy-bot: started job aorta-v1-q5-zwj-smoke-1777778888 (staging)

olga_petrov: Short-term mitigation: preprocess inputs in gateway to NFKC normalize and optionally strip ZWSP/ZWJ. Longer term: consider adding a quick grapheme normalization step in the fast tokenizer path or expose a build-time flag to keep exact behavior.

rahul_sinha: Also add a unit test that includes invisible chars in our tokenization CI (ZWSP, ZWJ, thin space, NBSP) and a regression check comparing qX outputs to fp16 baseline for a small subset.

mike_han: Any evidence of quant packer introducing pseudo-tokens? You said ids > vocab size: need to diff token->id maps pre/post pack. If packer reserved extension ids, ensure stable mapping.

sana_kobayashi: I diffed the raw vocab and token_map.json from the exporter: no new entries. So the runtime fast-path is creating different segmentation, then packer maps resulting token surface to extension slot id (hence high id).

olga_petrov: Action items: 1) short-term strip invisible chars in gateway and run full eval (sana). 2) eng-runtime: add opt-in normalize to qX fast path and a performance-tested variant (olga). 3) infra: add packer assert to catch id remap anomalies > vocab_size + 1024 (mike). 4) eng-ml: add multilingual invisible-char suite to nightly to catch retrieval regressions (rahul).

sana_kobayashi: Rolled gateway strip_zw_char=true to staging; retested sample: cosine for affected recovered to ~0.91 median and recall@10 recovered ~4.8 points. Filing INF-5180 "Invisible-joiner handling in qX fast-tokenize -> retrieval regressions" with repro and smoke job.

mike_han: Good. Please capture perf numbers for the gateway preproc (we saw ~0.25ms median per request added in load tests) so product/ops can evaluate. Also please attach the token diffs and the small script you used to run the smoke.

rahul_sinha: I'll add the CI tests and a nightly check. Also let's ensure we include a few RTL Arabic edgecases (ZWJ around diacritics) to avoid blindspots.

sana_kobayashi: TL;DR: root cause = fast-tokenize normalization off in qX builds -> invisible chars attached to preceding grapheme -> different token ids and embedding shifts -> retrieval degradation. Mitigation = strip/normalize in gateway + ticket to make normalization configurable in runtime. Rolling canary to Dedicated later today.

mike_han: Thanks team. Post INF-5180 link when ready and assign reviewers for runtime change.
